A01:2025.name: Broken Access Control
A01:2025.passive_scope: Permissive CORS response headers and sensitive paths advertised in robots.txt. Authorization logic itself requires authenticated manual testing.
A01:2025.description: Users can act outside their intended permissions: reading or changing other users' data, reaching admin functions, or calling APIs without the right authorization.

A02:2025.name: Security Misconfiguration
A02:2025.passive_scope: Missing or weak security headers, verbose banners, debug modes and missing security.txt.
A02:2025.description: The application, server or framework runs with insecure defaults, unneeded features, verbose errors or missing hardening.

A03:2025.name: Software Supply Chain Failures
A03:2025.passive_scope: Client-side JavaScript libraries fingerprinted from script URLs and matched against known-vulnerable versions. Server-side dependencies are not observable.
A03:2025.description: Vulnerable, unmaintained or compromised third-party components, dependencies or build pipelines end up in the running application.

manual_tests.title: CI/CD pipeline and artifact provenance review

A04:2025.name: Cryptographic Failures
A04:2025.passive_scope: Negotiated TLS protocol and cipher, certificate validity, HTTPS enforcement, HSTS, mixed content and cookie transport flags.
A04:2025.description: Sensitive data is exposed because encryption is missing, weak, misconfigured or relies on broken algorithms.

manual_tests.title: Encryption at rest and key management review

A05:2025.name: Injection
A05:2025.passive_scope: Only defense-in-depth indicators (CSP, X-Content-Type-Options). Injection flaws cannot be confirmed without active payloads, so a clean result requires manual review.
A05:2025.description: Untrusted input reaches an interpreter (SQL, OS shell, templates, browser DOM) and is executed as code or commands.

A06:2025.name: Insecure Design
A06:2025.passive_scope: Insecure form transport and missing anti-CSRF token patterns visible in HTML.
A06:2025.description: Flaws in the design itself, such as missing threat modelling, absent anti-automation or business logic that can be abused even when perfectly implemented.

manual_tests.title: Limits on how often a function can be used

A07:2025.name: Authentication Failures
A07:2025.passive_scope: Session cookie hardening, cleartext credential submission and caching of authenticated responses.
A07:2025.description: Weak login, session or credential handling lets attackers impersonate users: credential stuffing, weak passwords, session fixation or token theft.

A08:2025.name: Software or Data Integrity Failures
A08:2025.passive_scope: Third-party scripts and stylesheets loaded without Subresource Integrity.
A08:2025.description: Code or data is trusted without verifying its integrity: unsigned updates, unverified third-party scripts, insecure deserialization.

A09:2025.name: Security Logging and Alerting Failures
A09:2025.passive_scope: Not verifiable through passive HTTP/TLS inspection. Always flagged as Manual Review Required.
A09:2025.description: Security-relevant events are not logged, monitored or alerted on, so attacks go unnoticed.

manual_tests.title: Verify logins, access-control failures and input validation failures are logged with context
Verify alert thresholds and incident escalation
Review log retention and tamper protection

A10:2025.name: Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions
A10:2025.passive_scope: Raw stack traces, framework exception dumps and debug error pages returned in responses.
A10:2025.description: Errors and unusual conditions are handled unsafely: leaking internals, failing open, or leaving inconsistent state.

HDR-CSP-MISSING.title: Content-Security-Policy header missing
HDR-CSP-MISSING.description: The HTML response does not define a Content-Security-Policy. Without CSP the browser has no policy to restrict script sources, which removes an important mitigation against cross-site scripting and data injection.
HDR-CSP-MISSING.remediation: Deploy a restrictive Content-Security-Policy (start with default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self') and tighten it with nonces or hashes. Roll out using Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only first.

HDR-CSP-WEAK.title: Content-Security-Policy allows unsafe sources
HDR-CSP-WEAK.description: The Content-Security-Policy contains directives such as 'unsafe-inline', 'unsafe-eval', wildcard sources or plain http: sources in script-related directives, significantly reducing its effectiveness against XSS.
HDR-CSP-WEAK.remediation: Remove 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' from script-src/default-src, replace wildcards with explicit origins and use nonce- or hash-based allowlisting with 'strict-dynamic'.

HDR-HSTS-MISSING.title: Strict-Transport-Security header missing
HDR-HSTS-MISSING.description: The HTTPS response does not include a Strict-Transport-Security header. Users who type the bare hostname or follow http:// links can be downgraded by an on-path attacker (SSL stripping).
HDR-HSTS-MISSING.remediation: Send 'Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains' on every HTTPS response and consider HSTS preloading once all subdomains support HTTPS.

HDR-HSTS-WEAK.title: Strict-Transport-Security max-age too short
HDR-HSTS-WEAK.description: The Strict-Transport-Security policy uses a max-age below 180 days (15552000 seconds) or disables HSTS with max-age=0, giving only brief or no protection against protocol downgrade.
HDR-HSTS-WEAK.remediation: Increase max-age to at least 31536000 (one year) and include includeSubDomains where possible.

HDR-XFO-MISSING.title: Clickjacking protection missing (X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors)
HDR-XFO-MISSING.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames
HDR-XFO-MISSING.description: The HTML response sets neither X-Frame-Options nor a CSP frame-ancestors directive, so the page may be framed by any origin and abused for clickjacking.

HDR-XCTO-MISSING.title: X-Content-Type-Options header missing
HDR-XCTO-MISSING.description: The response does not include 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff'. Browsers may MIME-sniff responses and interpret user-controlled content as script or HTML.
HDR-XCTO-MISSING.remediation: Send 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' on all responses and ensure accurate Content-Type headers.

HDR-REFERRER-MISSING.title: Referrer-Policy header missing
HDR-REFERRER-MISSING.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
HDR-REFERRER-MISSING.description: No Referrer-Policy is defined. Modern browsers default to strict-origin-when-cross-origin, but older clients may leak full URLs (including tokens in query strings) to third parties.
HDR-REFERRER-MISSING.remediation: Send 'Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin' or 'no-referrer' for sensitive applications.

HDR-PERMISSIONS-MISSING.title: Permissions-Policy header missing
HDR-PERMISSIONS-MISSING.description: No Permissions-Policy is defined, so powerful browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation, payment) are not explicitly restricted for this origin and embedded frames.
HDR-PERMISSIONS-MISSING.remediation: Send a Permissions-Policy disabling unused features, e.g. 'Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=()'.

TLS-NO-HTTPS.title: HTTPS not available
TLS-NO-HTTPS.description: The host serves content over plain HTTP but no working HTTPS endpoint was observed. All traffic, including cookies and credentials, travels in cleartext.
TLS-NO-HTTPS.remediation: Provision a valid TLS certificate, serve the application exclusively over HTTPS and redirect all HTTP requests with a 301 to the HTTPS origin.

TLS-NO-REDIRECT.title: HTTP does not redirect to HTTPS
TLS-NO-REDIRECT.description: The plain HTTP endpoint returns content instead of redirecting to HTTPS, allowing users to browse the application unencrypted.
TLS-NO-REDIRECT.remediation: Return a 301/308 redirect from every http:// URL to the equivalent https:// URL and enable HSTS.

TLS-DEPRECATED-PROTOCOL.title: Deprecated TLS protocol supported
TLS-DEPRECATED-PROTOCOL.description: The server negotiated or accepted TLS 1.0/1.1 (or older). These protocols are deprecated by RFC 8996 and lack modern cryptographic protections.
TLS-DEPRECATED-PROTOCOL.remediation: Disable SSLv3, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1. Support TLS 1.2 with AEAD cipher suites and TLS 1.3.

TLS-WEAK-CIPHER.title: Weak TLS cipher suite negotiated
TLS-WEAK-CIPHER.cwe_name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
TLS-WEAK-CIPHER.description: The cipher suite negotiated with a standard client uses a broken or legacy algorithm (RC4, DES/3DES, NULL, EXPORT, anonymous key exchange or MD5) or an effective key length below 128 bits.
TLS-WEAK-CIPHER.remediation: Restrict the server to AEAD cipher suites (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305) with forward secrecy (ECDHE).

TLS-CERT-EXPIRED.title: TLS certificate expired or not yet valid
TLS-CERT-EXPIRED.description: The certificate presented by the server is outside its validity window. Browsers show interstitial warnings, training users to click through certificate errors.
TLS-CERT-EXPIRED.remediation: Renew the certificate immediately and automate renewal (e.g. ACME) with expiry monitoring.

TLS-CERT-EXPIRING.title: TLS certificate expires within 30 days
TLS-CERT-EXPIRING.description: The server certificate will expire soon. Unless renewed, users will receive certificate errors and service availability will be impacted.
TLS-CERT-EXPIRING.remediation: Renew the certificate and ensure automated renewal with alerting at least 30 days before expiry.

TLS-CERT-HOSTNAME-MISMATCH.title: TLS certificate hostname mismatch
TLS-CERT-HOSTNAME-MISMATCH.cwe_name: Improper Validation of Certificate with Host Mismatch
TLS-CERT-HOSTNAME-MISMATCH.description: None of the certificate's Subject Alternative Names (or Common Name) match the audited hostname, so clients cannot authenticate the server.
TLS-CERT-HOSTNAME-MISMATCH.remediation: Issue a certificate whose SAN list covers this hostname (or an appropriate wildcard) and deploy it on the correct virtual host / SNI configuration.

TLS-CERT-UNTRUSTED.title: TLS certificate not trusted
TLS-CERT-UNTRUSTED.description: The certificate chain could not be validated against the public trust store (self-signed, unknown issuer or incomplete chain).
TLS-CERT-UNTRUSTED.remediation: Deploy a certificate issued by a publicly trusted CA and serve the complete intermediate chain.

TLS-MIXED-CONTENT-ACTIVE.title: Active mixed content (scripts/frames/styles over HTTP)
TLS-MIXED-CONTENT-ACTIVE.description: The HTTPS page references scripts, stylesheets, iframes or other active resources over plain http://. An on-path attacker can tamper with these resources and take over the page.
TLS-MIXED-CONTENT-ACTIVE.remediation: Load every sub-resource over https:// and add 'Content-Security-Policy: upgrade-insecure-requests' as a safety net.

TLS-MIXED-CONTENT-PASSIVE.title: Passive mixed content (images/media over HTTP)
TLS-MIXED-CONTENT-PASSIVE.description: The HTTPS page references images, audio or video over plain http://, leaking browsing activity and allowing content spoofing.
TLS-MIXED-CONTENT-PASSIVE.remediation: Serve all media over https:// and enable 'upgrade-insecure-requests'.

CKE-NO-SECURE.title: Cookie without Secure flag
CKE-NO-SECURE.cwe_name: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
CKE-NO-SECURE.description: A cookie is issued without the Secure attribute, so the browser will also transmit it over unencrypted HTTP connections where it can be intercepted.
CKE-NO-SECURE.remediation: Set the Secure attribute on all cookies, and use the __Host- prefix for session cookies.

CKE-SESSION-NO-HTTPONLY.title: Session cookie without HttpOnly flag
CKE-SESSION-NO-HTTPONLY.description: A cookie whose name indicates a session or authentication token lacks the HttpOnly attribute, so any cross-site scripting flaw can steal it via document.cookie.
CKE-SESSION-NO-HTTPONLY.remediation: Set HttpOnly on all session and authentication cookies.

CKE-NO-HTTPONLY.title: Cookie without HttpOnly flag
CKE-NO-HTTPONLY.description: A cookie is issued without the HttpOnly attribute and is readable from JavaScript. If it carries sensitive state it can be stolen through XSS.
CKE-NO-HTTPONLY.remediation: Set HttpOnly on every cookie that does not need to be read by client-side script.

CKE-NO-SAMESITE.title: Cookie without SameSite attribute
CKE-NO-SAMESITE.cwe_name: Sensitive Cookie with Improper SameSite Attribute
CKE-NO-SAMESITE.description: A cookie is issued without an explicit SameSite attribute. Browser defaults vary, and older clients will attach it to cross-site requests, increasing CSRF exposure.
CKE-NO-SAMESITE.remediation: Set SameSite=Lax (or Strict for highly sensitive cookies) explicitly on every cookie.

CKE-SAMESITE-NONE-INSECURE.title: SameSite=None cookie without Secure
CKE-SAMESITE-NONE-INSECURE.cwe_name: Sensitive Cookie with Improper SameSite Attribute
CKE-SAMESITE-NONE-INSECURE.description: A cookie declares SameSite=None without the Secure attribute. Modern browsers reject it; legacy browsers send it cross-site and over cleartext HTTP.
CKE-SAMESITE-NONE-INSECURE.remediation: Always pair SameSite=None with Secure, or use SameSite=Lax if cross-site delivery is not required.

CKE-BROAD-DOMAIN.title: Cookie scoped to parent domain
CKE-BROAD-DOMAIN.cwe_name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
CKE-BROAD-DOMAIN.description: A cookie's Domain attribute is set to a parent domain, so it will be sent to every sibling subdomain. A compromise of any less-secure subdomain exposes or allows overwriting of this cookie.
CKE-BROAD-DOMAIN.remediation: Omit the Domain attribute (host-only cookie) or use the __Host- prefix so the cookie is only sent to the issuing host.

CORS-WILDCARD-CREDENTIALS.title: CORS wildcard origin combined with credentials
CORS-WILDCARD-CREDENTIALS.cwe_name: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains
CORS-WILDCARD-CREDENTIALS.description: The response sends 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' together with 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true'. Browsers refuse this combination, which typically indicates a CORS layer that will be 'fixed' by reflecting arbitrary origins.
CORS-WILDCARD-CREDENTIALS.remediation: Maintain a strict allowlist of trusted origins and only return Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true for those exact origins.

CORS-NULL-ORIGIN.title: CORS trusts the null origin
CORS-NULL-ORIGIN.cwe_name: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains
CORS-NULL-ORIGIN.description: The response returns 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null'. Sandboxed iframes and data: URLs from any attacker page carry the null origin and can read the response.
CORS-NULL-ORIGIN.remediation: Never allowlist the null origin; return only explicit trusted origins.

CORS-WILDCARD.title: CORS allows any origin
CORS-WILDCARD.cwe_name: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains
CORS-WILDCARD.description: The response is readable cross-origin by any website ('Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *'). This is safe for genuinely public content but must not be applied to responses containing user-specific or internal data.
CORS-WILDCARD.remediation: Confirm the resource is public. Otherwise replace the wildcard with an explicit origin allowlist.

CACHE-SENSITIVE-NO-STORE.title: Sensitive response cacheable (missing Cache-Control: no-store)
CACHE-SENSITIVE-NO-STORE.cwe_name: Use of Web Browser Cache Containing Sensitive Information
CACHE-SENSITIVE-NO-STORE.description: A response that sets session cookies or contains a login form does not prevent caching. Shared proxies or browser history on shared machines may retain sensitive content.
CACHE-SENSITIVE-NO-STORE.remediation: Send 'Cache-Control: no-store' (and 'Pragma: no-cache' for HTTP/1.0 caches) on authenticated and credential-handling responses.

DISC-SERVER-VERSION.title: Server version disclosed in banner
DISC-SERVER-VERSION.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
DISC-SERVER-VERSION.description: The Server header reveals the product and exact version, letting attackers quickly match the host against known vulnerabilities.
DISC-SERVER-VERSION.remediation: Suppress version details (e.g. nginx 'server_tokens off;', Apache 'ServerTokens Prod' / 'ServerSignature Off').

DISC-VERSION-HEADER.title: Technology version disclosed in response header
DISC-VERSION-HEADER.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
DISC-VERSION-HEADER.description: Headers such as X-Powered-By, X-AspNet-Version, X-AspNetMvc-Version or X-Generator reveal the application framework and version.
DISC-VERSION-HEADER.remediation: Remove framework identification headers (e.g. Express 'app.disable("x-powered-by")', PHP 'expose_php = Off', ASP.NET 'enableVersionHeader="false"').

DISC-STACK-TRACE.title: Stack trace or exception dump disclosed
DISC-STACK-TRACE.cwe_name: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
DISC-STACK-TRACE.description: The response body contains a raw stack trace or framework exception dump, revealing internal file paths, code structure, library versions and sometimes data values.
DISC-STACK-TRACE.remediation: Handle exceptions centrally, return generic error pages to clients and log the full details server-side only.

DISC-DEBUG-MODE.title: Debug mode or developer tooling exposed
DISC-DEBUG-MODE.description: The response shows signs of a framework running in debug/development mode (Django DEBUG page, Werkzeug debugger, Laravel Ignition/Whoops, Symfony profiler, Rails debug exception page or X-Debug-Token headers).
DISC-DEBUG-MODE.remediation: Disable debug mode in production deployments and remove developer toolbars and profilers.

DISC-HTML-COMMENTS.title: Sensitive developer comments in HTML
DISC-HTML-COMMENTS.cwe_name: Inclusion of Sensitive Information in Source Code Comments
DISC-HTML-COMMENTS.description: HTML comments contain developer notes mentioning credentials, internal hosts, debugging or unfinished security work.
DISC-HTML-COMMENTS.remediation: Strip comments from production HTML in the build pipeline and never place secrets or internal notes in client-delivered markup.

DISC-PRIVATE-IP.title: Private IP address disclosed
DISC-PRIVATE-IP.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
DISC-PRIVATE-IP.description: An RFC 1918 private IP address appears in the response headers or body, revealing internal network addressing.
DISC-PRIVATE-IP.remediation: Remove internal addresses from responses; review reverse proxy headers and templated configuration values.

DISC-EMAIL.title: Email addresses disclosed
DISC-EMAIL.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
DISC-EMAIL.description: Email addresses appear in the page content. They can be harvested for phishing and social engineering.
DISC-EMAIL.remediation: Confirm each published address is intended to be public; prefer role-based aliases or contact forms.

FORM-PASSWORD-OVER-HTTP.title: Cleartext submission of password
FORM-PASSWORD-OVER-HTTP.description: A form containing a password field is served over HTTP or submits to an http:// action, exposing credentials to network attackers.
FORM-PASSWORD-OVER-HTTP.remediation: Serve login pages exclusively over HTTPS and ensure form actions use https:// (or relative URLs on an HTTPS page).

FORM-INSECURE-ACTION.title: Form submits to insecure HTTP endpoint
FORM-INSECURE-ACTION.description: An HTML form on an HTTPS page submits its data to an http:// URL, downgrading the user's input to cleartext.
FORM-INSECURE-ACTION.remediation: Change form actions to https:// or relative URLs.

FORM-NO-CSRF-TOKEN.title: State-changing form without anti-CSRF token
FORM-NO-CSRF-TOKEN.description: A POST form does not contain a hidden field matching common anti-CSRF token names. Unless protected by SameSite cookies or custom headers, it may be vulnerable to cross-site request forgery. Requires manual confirmation.
FORM-NO-CSRF-TOKEN.remediation: Add a per-session or per-request synchronizer token to all state-changing forms and validate it server-side; also set SameSite on session cookies.

FORM-PASSWORD-AUTOCOMPLETE.title: Password field with autocomplete enabled
FORM-PASSWORD-AUTOCOMPLETE.description: A password input does not set an autocomplete hint. Browsers may store the value; on shared workstations this can expose credentials. Modern guidance permits password managers, so treat as informational.
FORM-PASSWORD-AUTOCOMPLETE.remediation: Use autocomplete="current-password" / "new-password" to cooperate with password managers, or autocomplete="off" for high-risk shared-terminal contexts.

SRI-MISSING-SCRIPT.title: External script without Subresource Integrity
SRI-MISSING-SCRIPT.description: A script is loaded from a third-party origin without an integrity attribute. If the CDN or host is compromised, malicious code runs with full access to this origin.
SRI-MISSING-SCRIPT.remediation: Add integrity="sha384-..." and crossorigin="anonymous" to third-party scripts, or self-host them.

SRI-MISSING-STYLESHEET.title: External stylesheet without Subresource Integrity
SRI-MISSING-STYLESHEET.description: A stylesheet is loaded from a third-party origin without an integrity attribute. A compromised host could inject CSS used for UI redressing or data exfiltration.
SRI-MISSING-STYLESHEET.remediation: Add integrity and crossorigin attributes to third-party stylesheets or self-host them.

JS-VULNERABLE-LIBRARY.title: Vulnerable JavaScript library version
JS-VULNERABLE-LIBRARY.description: A client-side library version inferred from the script URL is affected by publicly known vulnerabilities. Version is fingerprinted passively from the filename/path and should be confirmed.
JS-VULNERABLE-LIBRARY.remediation: Upgrade the library to a supported, patched release and track client-side dependencies with an SCA tool (npm audit, Retire.js, Dependabot).

META-SECURITY-TXT-MISSING.title: security.txt not published
META-SECURITY-TXT-MISSING.description: No RFC 9116 security.txt file was found at /.well-known/security.txt, so researchers have no documented channel to report vulnerabilities.
META-SECURITY-TXT-MISSING.remediation: Publish /.well-known/security.txt with at least Contact and Expires fields, ideally signed and including a Policy link.

META-SECURITY-TXT-INVALID.title: security.txt incomplete or expired
META-SECURITY-TXT-INVALID.description: The security.txt file is missing the required Contact or Expires field, or its Expires date has passed (RFC 9116 section 2.5).
META-SECURITY-TXT-INVALID.remediation: Add the required Contact and Expires fields and keep the expiry date current (less than one year ahead).

META-ROBOTS-SENSITIVE.title: robots.txt reveals sensitive paths
META-ROBOTS-SENSITIVE.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
META-ROBOTS-SENSITIVE.description: robots.txt Disallow entries advertise administrative, backup, configuration or internal paths. robots.txt is not an access control and acts as a roadmap for attackers. (WAPTrix does not request these paths.)
META-ROBOTS-SENSITIVE.remediation: Protect sensitive paths with authentication and network controls; avoid listing them in robots.txt.

headers.name: Security headers
headers.method: Reads the security headers (and any CSP meta tag) on the final response to GET /. Parses CSP directives and the HSTS max-age.

transport_tls.name: Transport & TLS
transport_tls.method: Compares GET / over HTTP and HTTPS, including redirect chains. Inspects three TLS handshakes: one to read the certificate, one validated against the certifi CA bundle, and one ClientHello capped at TLS 1.1. Scans the HTML for http:// sub-resources.

cookies.name: Cookies
cookies.method: Parses every Set-Cookie header on all responses and redirect hops and flags missing attributes. Cookie values are redacted in evidence.

cors_cache.name: CORS & caching
cors_cache.method: Reviews CORS headers returned to a normal GET (no Origin header is sent), and Cache-Control on responses that set session cookies or contain a password field.

disclosure.name: Information disclosure
disclosure.method: Matches response headers and bodies against version-banner, stack-trace, debug-page, private-IP and email patterns. Reviews HTML comments for sensitive keywords.

client_forms.name: Forms & client-side
client_forms.method: Parses HTML forms (action scheme, method, hidden CSRF fields, password inputs) and script/link tags (integrity attribute, third-party origin, versioned library URLs matched against known-vulnerable ranges).

metadata.name: Security metadata
metadata.method: Fetches /robots.txt and /.well-known/security.txt. Validates the RFC 9116 fields and lists sensitive Disallow entries without requesting them.
